title: Password changed on the laptop, phone Outlook still asks for it

review.authored_by: claude-opus-5 (Claude Code session) — drafted from the runbooks, the triage prompt's definitions and decide.ts, not from system output

input.subject: Outlook on my phone keeps asking for my password

conversation.author: requester
conversation.body:
Hi,

My password expired this morning and I changed it when the laptop prompted me. The laptop is fine now, but Outlook on my phone keeps asking for my password and won't take the new one.

Thanks,
Tom

triage.subcategory: cached password on phone after expiry

irrelevant: Setting up MFA on a new phone

must_include.what: Sign out of Outlook (and Teams) on the phone, then sign back in with the new password

must_not_include.what: Tells him to reset or re-register MFA
Tells him to reset the password again

characteristics: One or two numbered steps; the laptop needs nothing
Says the phone holds the old password until it signs out

rationale: Step 5 of the password runbook is exactly this: the old password stays cached on mobile until the account signs out and back in. He can work on the laptop, so P3. A routine expiry is not a credential compromise, so not security-sensitive (guideline G3). The MFA runbook would send him down the wrong path.
